turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, this is Arjun, four years old, come with his mother and grandfather. Temperature just now is 38.8 Celsius, pulse 126 per minute, respiratory rate 26 per minute, and saturation 98 percent.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Sit comfortably, both of you. Arjun beta, what has been happening?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ma'am, he is having fever and cough. From two days he is not himself, and he is not eating properly also.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two days? It is four days. The cough started Sunday night, you were at your sister's place.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Well, actually I thought it was Tuesday. Um, two days only I am telling you, and last night it touched 102.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It was 100 on the thermometer, not 102. You add on when you get frightened.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, so we will keep it as roughly two to four days, you are not matching on that, or on how high it went at home. How is the cough?
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Dry cough, worse in the night, he wakes up. Daytime it is on and off.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting, loose motions, rash?
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, no rash. Stools are normal.
[SEG0011] person_5 (PATIENT): Are you going to poke me?
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): No poke, beta. Does your tummy hurt?
[SEG0013] person_5 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is he drinking, and passing urine?
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Drinking little little. Urine has come about four times, and he is not pulling his ear.
[SEG0016] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the medicine, tell it properly.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I gave Crocin syrup, one small spoon, the fever syrup. Three times yesterday, two in the day and, um, one at night.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That was not the small spoon, it was the big spoon, I watched you. At night I also gave Ibugesic, half a spoon, the pink one, because fever was staying.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I didn't know about Ibugesic. I only gave the Crocin.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted. Any fast breathing, chest pulling in?
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, nothing like that. He even played with his car for a bit.
[SEG0022] person_5 (PATIENT): Will medicine be yucky? Can we go home?
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Home soon, and we will pick a medicine that is not too bad. Open your mouth for me, I am only looking.
[SEG0024] person_5 (PATIENT): It hurts?
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): No hurt. Throat is a little red. Ears look fine.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, no wheeze, no crackles. Tummy is soft.
[SEG0027] person_5 (PATIENT): Mama, my tummy is paining.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He never said that at home. Now only he is telling.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Show me, beta, where?
[SEG0030] person_5 (PATIENT): Here. Tummy.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): I don't find any guarding. Most likely a viral fever with cough. I cannot fully rule out an early chest infection, but the chest is clear today.
[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Cousin had dengue last month, no? Should we do blood test? I kept thinking in the auto.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the fever is still high after three days, or he is very dull, then we might do a blood count.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Which syrup do I continue, Crocin or the pink one? Spoon size I am not sure anymore.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): No more kitchen spoons. I will write paracetamol syrup 5 ml by mouth, up to four times a day if fever is there, gap of at least four hours. Don't give ibuprofen as well unless I say, and offer small sips of water often.
[SEG0036] person_5 (PATIENT): Am I sick? Can I go school?
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): A little sick, so rest at home, no school tomorrow. School once the fever is gone and the cough is better.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If he worsens at night, what do I do? I will be so worried.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): If he is breathing fast, not drinking at all, or fever not coming down with the syrup, go to emergency. Otherwise, if he is not better in three days, come back and see me.
[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I have my purple inhaler in the bag for my asthma. One puff for him?
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, please, that is your inhaler, not his. Sister, can you print the dose for them?
[SEG0042] person_1 (NURSE): Yes doctor, I will print the syrup slip at the desk now.
